question: Should omitted `plugins.entries.active-memory.config.agents` activate Active Memory for every configured agent or `main` on upgrade, or should this branch be narrowed to the single-agent command parity bug?
rationale: The code path is clear, but the omitted-agent default changes a compatibility-sensitive plugin targeting contract that repository policy leaves to maintainer intent.

options.title: Narrow Before Merge
options.body: Preserve current omitted-agent behavior by default and fix the linked single-agent command issue through a narrower command parity, setup, docs, or doctor path.

options.title: Approve New Default
options.body: Accept omission as configured agents or `main`, with this PR's docs/tests as the upgrade contract and explicit `agents: []` as the opt-out.

options.title: Pause Or Close Direction
options.body: If Active Memory targeting must remain explicit, pause or close this branch and keep the narrower bug/design discussion on the canonical issue.

recommendation.title: Narrow Before Merge
recommendation.body: Preserve current omitted-agent behavior by default and fix the linked single-agent command issue through a narrower command parity, setup, docs, or doctor path.

likelyOwner.reason: Takhoffman introduced Active Memory and carried major follow-up behavior work, making them the strongest history-based owner for the targeting-default decision.
